newsitem.title: CHINA: Industrial accidents decline in China.
newsitem.headline: Industrial accidents decline in China.

text.p: China saw a sharp fall in the number of industrial accidents in the first half of this year with fewer people killed in mining disasters but a higher death toll on the railways, the China Daily said on Monday.
The Ministry of Labour reported 5,737 industrial accidents in the first half, down 12.8 percent year-on-year, while the death toll reached 6,117, a decline of 8.6 percent, it said.
Major accidents totalled 296, leaving 2,058 people dead or declines of 15.4 percent and 1.8 percent, respectively.
Of the major accidents, 233 occurred in mining organisations, down 18 percent year-on-year, while the death toll fell by 2.2 percent to 1,708, it said.
The number of accidents involving units under the Ministry of Communications fell by four percent to 362 and the number of deaths was down by 8.9 percent to 247, it said.

However, accidents in the railway sector left 98 people dead, a large increase over last year, it said without giving comparative figures. The dead were killed when two trains collided in central Hunan province in April in one of the worst rail accidents in China in recent years.
Aviation accidents left 37 people dead, the ministry report said. All were apparently killed when a China Southern Airlines Boeing 737 crashed in the southern town of Shenzhen in May.
China issued an urgent circular after those two accidents calling for better transport safety and a nationwide inspection of accident-prone industries.
